desc: Indexed from 1, 100 is fully deployed, 0 flat on deck

name: CABLE CAUGHT BY TAILHOOK:index
desc: A number 1 through 4 for the cable number caught by the tailhook. Cable 1 is the one closest to the stern of the carrier. A value of 0 indicates no cable was caught.

name: CATAPULT STROKE POSITION:index
desc: Catapults are indexed from 1. This value will be 0 before the catapult fires, and then up to 100 as the aircraft is propelled down the catapult. The aircraft may takeoff before the value reaches 100 (depending on the aircraft weight, power applied, and other factors), in which case this value will not be further updated. This value could be used to drive a bogie animation.

name: HOLDBACK BAR INSTALLED
desc: Holdback bars allow build up of thrust before takeoff from a catapult, and are installed by the deck crew of an aircraft carrier.

name: LAUNCHBAR HELD EXTENDED
desc: This will be True if the launchbar is fully extended, and can be used, for example, to change the color of an instrument light.

name: LAUNCHBAR POSITION
desc: Installed on aircraft before takeoff from a carrier catapult. Note that gear cannot retract with this extended. 100 = fully extended.

name: LAUNCHBAR SWITCH
desc: If this is set to True the launch bar switch has been engaged.

name: NUMBER OF CATAPULTS
desc: Maximum of 4. A model can contain more than 4 catapults, but only the first four will be read and recognized by the simulation.

name: CONCORDE NOSE ANGLE
desc: The nose angle, where 0 is fully up.

name: CONCORDE VISOR NOSE HANDLE

name: CONCORDE VISOR POSITION PERCENT
desc: The visor position expressed as a percentage where 0.0 = up and 1.0 = extended/down.

name: BUS LOOKUP INDEX:1
desc: This SimVar is used only by the v1.00 electrical system and is used to supply a Bus index to another SimVar (see here for more information); It should be noted that when this is not set (ie: it is 0) then TRUE will be returned if any of the bus connections are on.; IMPORTANT! This SimVar is deprecated as you can now simply supply two indices to the SimVars that used it. [indexed (v1.00: Bus index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: BUS BREAKER PULLED:1
desc: This will be true if the bus breaker is pulled. For the v2+ electrical system it requires the name (or index) of the Bus , while the legacy v1.00 electrical system requires two Bus indices. This SimVar cannot be used with the FSX electrical system. [indexed (v2+: Bus name (or index) ; v1.00: First bus index; Second bus index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: BUS CONNECTION ON:1
desc: This will be True if the line between the two buses is connected. For the v2+ electrical system it requires the names (or indices) of the Buses to check, and the legacy v1.00 electrical system needs the Bus indices. This SimVar cannot be used with the FSX electrical system. [indexed (v2+: First bus name (or index); Second bus name (or index) ; v1.00: First bus index; Second bus index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL BUS AMPS:1

name: ELECTRICAL BUS VOLTAGE:1
desc: Returns the tension going through the named (or indexed) Bus , in volts.; Note that if you supply an index it is the global index, ie: the index N of the circuit parameter itself.; This is only available to the modern (v2+) electrical system. [indexed (v2+: Bus name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: NEW ELECTRICAL SYSTEM
desc: Is the aircraft using the modern v2+ or v1.00 electrical system ( True ), or the old FSX electrical system ( False ).

name: ELECTRICAL AVIONICS BUS AMPS
desc: Avionics bus current.; This is a legacy SimVar, only used by the FSX electrical system. For the v2+ system, use ELECTRICAL BUS AMPS (there is no equivalent for the v1.00 system). [settable]

name: ELECTRICAL AVIONICS BUS VOLTAGE

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY BUS AMPS:1
desc: Battery bus current.; This is a legacy SimVar, only used by the FSX and v1.00 electrical systems. For the v2+ system (and preferrably for the v1.00 system as well), use ELECTRICAL BUS AMPS . [indexed (v1.00+: Battery index ; FSX: N/A): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY BUS VOLTAGE:1
desc: Battery bus voltage.; This is a legacy SimVar, only used by the FSX and v1.00 electrical systems. For the v2+ system (and preferrably for the v1.00 system as well) use ELECTRICAL BUS VOLTAGE . [indexed (v1.00+: Battery index ; FSX: N/A): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL GENALT BUS AMPS:1
desc: The load handled by the indexed generator bus.; For the modern (v2+) electrical system, use ELECTRICAL BUS AMPS .; [indexed (v1.00+ / FSX: Generator index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL GENALT BUS VOLTAGE:1

name: ELECTRICAL MAIN BUS AMPS:1

name: ELECTRICAL MAIN BUS VOLTAGE:1
desc: The main named (or indexed) Bus voltage.; For the modern (v2+) electrical system, use ELECTRICAL BUS VOLTAGE . [indexed (v1.00: Bus index ; FSX: N/A (main bus is hardcoded)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL OLD CHARGING AMPS:1

name: BATTERY BREAKER PULLED:1
desc: This will be true if the battery breaker is pulled. For the v2+ electrical system it simply requires the Battery name (or index), while the legacy v1.00 electrical system requires a Battery index and a Bus index. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00: Battery index; Bus index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: BATTERY CONNECTION ON:1

For the v2+ electrical system it simply requires the Battery name (or index), while the legacy v1.00 electrical system requires a Battery index and a Bus index. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00: Battery index; Bus index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY ESTIMATED CAPACITY PCT:1
desc: The remaing capacity of the named (or indexed) Battery .; Note that for the FSX and legacy (v1.00) electrical systems, requests to this SimVar must be done in Percent Over 100 as conversions will not work. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00 / FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …]

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY LEVEL:1
desc: The remaining capacity of the named (or indexed) Battery , expressed as a percentage.; This is only available to the modern (v2+) electrical system. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00 / FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY LOAD:1
desc: For the FSX and legacy (v1.00) electrical systems, this is the load handled by the indexed battery, where negative values mean the battery is receiving current.; For the modern (v2+) electrical system, this is the load drawn from the Battery when it is used as a supplier , and will not return the supplied tension when charging, or when the battery is not a supplier. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00 / FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL BATTERY VOLTAGE:1
desc: For the FSX and legacy (v1.00) electrical systems, this is the tension output of the indexed battery.; For the modern (v2+) electrical system, this is the tension output for a Battery that is used as a supplier , and will not return the supplied tension when charging. Note that if the battery is not a supplier, the tension will always be 0. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00 / FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL HOT BATTERY BUS AMPS:1
desc: Load available when the battery switch is turned off .; This is only valid for the FSX electrical system. [indexed (FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL HOT BATTERY BUS VOLTAGE:1
desc: Tension available when the battery switch is turned off .; This is only valid for the FSX electrical system. [indexed (FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: ELECTRICAL MASTER BATTERY:1
desc: The named (or indexed) Battery switch position, True if the switch is on . There are some things to notw about using an index of 0 with this parameter based on the electrical system version being used:; FSX : GET 0 (like 1) is the first battery. SET 0 is every battery.; Legacy v1.00 : GET 0 indicates if any battery is on. SET 0 (and 1) sets the switch of the first battery.; Modern v2+ : GET 0 indicates if *any *battery is on. SET 0 sets the switch of every batteries like FSX. [indexed (v2+: Battery name (or index) ; v1.00 / FSX: Battery index): :1, :2 …; settable]

TURB ENG THROTTLE COMMANDED N1 is also updated with the same value.; - When false , which is the default, commanded Ne continues to be calculated internally by the turbine engine code, so the existing behavior remains unchanged. ; NOTE : This SimVar will not accept an index of 0, and each engine must be specified individually. [indexed (Engine Index 💡︎): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: TURB ENG CONDITION LEVER POSITION:1

[indexed (Engine Index 💡︎): :1, :2 …; 0 = fuel cut-off; 1 = low idle; 2 = high idle; settable]

name: DESIGN SPEED VC
desc: This design constant represents the aircraft ideal cruising speed. It is derived from the cruise_speed setting in the [REFERENCE SPEEDS] section of the flight_model.cfg . The default value is computed an internal function that uses the estimated cruise altitude and estimated cruise percent power, according of the engine type, the number of engines, the density, the wing area and some drag parameters. Normally this value is set in the CFG file and the default value is never used.

name: DESIGN SPEED VS0
desc: This design constant represents the the stall speed when flaps are fully extended. It is derived from the full_flaps_stall_speed setting in the [REFERENCE SPEEDS] section of the flight_model.cfg . Default value is 0.8 x VS.

name: DESIGN SPEED VS1
desc: This design constant represents the stall speed when flaps are fully retracted. It is derived from the flaps_up_stall_speed setting in the [REFERENCE SPEEDS] section of the flight_model.cfg . Default value is 0.

name: DESIGN TAKEOFF SPEED
desc: This design constant represents the aircraft ideal takoff speed. It is derived from the takeoff_speed setting in the [REFERENCE SPEEDS] section of the flight_model.cfg .

name: WEAR AND TEAR CHECK PROGRESSION:1
desc: This SimVar is only valid during the pre-flight inspection phase of a flight, it is used to get (or set) the timer used for the inspection interaction (the circular progress bar) with a particular component. The component is identified by the given component ID/name and index.; See the Wear And Tear Component IDs section for a full list of component names/IDs. [indexed ([0] Component ID; [1] Optional Component Index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: WEAR AND TEAR EXPOSED PARTS LEVEL
desc: This SimVar returns the average wear and tear level of the exposed parts of the aircraft. The SimVar does not take any ID or index, as it is based on an internal calculation which takes data from multiple different sources, like the control surfaces, engines, etc… The SimVar returns a value between 0 and 1 where a 1 means that the aircraft is fully functional and undamaged, and a value of 0 means that the aircraft is seriously damaged and potentially unflyable.

name: WEAR AND TEAR EXPOSED PARTS LOWEST LEVEL
desc: This SimVar returns the lowest wear and tear level of the exposed parts of the aircraft. The SimVar does not take any ID or index, as it is based on an internal calculation which takes data from multiple different sources, like the control surfaces, engines, etc… The SimVar returns a value between 0 and 1 where a 1 means that the aircraft is fully functional and undamaged, and a value of 0 means that the aircraft is seriously damaged and potentially unflyable.

name: WEAR AND TEAR IS FAILED:1
desc: This SimVar will return TRUE (1) if the given component ID/name has failed completely, ie: it’s “health” has fallen to zero and the component is considered by the simulation as “broken”. If the component is still functioning, regardless of how “weak” it may be, then this will return FALSE (1).; See the Wear And Tear Component IDs section for a full list of component names/IDs. [indexed ([0] Component ID; [1] Optional Component Index): :1, :2 …]

name: WEAR AND TEAR IS WEAK:1
desc: This SimVar will return TRUE (1) if the given component ID/name is considered as being “weak”, ie: it’s “health” has fallen to a point where it could fail or break, and the compònent may have reduced functionality. If the component is not considered as “weak” (even if its wear and tear value is less than 1), then this will return FALSE (1).; See the Wear And Tear Component IDs section for a full list of component names/IDs. [indexed ([0] Component ID; [1] Optional Component Index): :1, :2 …]

name: WEAR AND TEAR LEVEL:1
desc: This SimVar returns the current wear and tear level of the component or system being referenced, where a value of 1 is a fully functional and undamaged component, and a value of 0 means that the component has failed. The SimVar requires an ID value or name, and may also use an additional index value to tell the simulation exactly which one of the components of the given type you are targeting.; See the Wear And Tear Component IDs section for a full list of component names/IDs. [indexed ([0] Component ID; [1] Optional Component Index): :1, :2 …]

name: WEAR AND TEAR WEAK VALUE:1
desc: This SimVar returns the current “weakness” level of the component or system being referenced, where a value of 1 is a fully functional (but not necessarily undamaged) component, and a value of 0 means that the component has failed. If this value is less than 1, then the component will experience reduced functionality and may also be more prone to failure and breaking.; The SimVar requires an ID value or name, and may also use an additional index value to tell the simulation exactly which one of the components of the given type you are targeting. See the Wear And Tear Component IDs section for a full list of component names/IDs. [indexed ([0] Component ID; [1] Optional Component Index): :1, :2 …]

It can also be modified using the ground_crosswind_effect_zero_speed and ground_crosswind_effect_max_speed parameters to ease taxiing and takeoff by design for an aircraft.

name: AIRCRAFT WIND Z

name: NAV DMESPEED

name: NAV FREQUENCY
desc: Localizer course frequency.

name: NAV GLIDE SLOPE
desc: The glide slope gradient. The value returned is an integer value formed as follows:; sin(slope) 65536 2 ; So, for example, a glide slope of 2.7º would return a value of 6174. TO get the value in degrees, then use NAV RAW GLIDE SLOPE instead.

desc: Difference between current position and glideslope angle. Note that this provides 32 bit floating point precision, rather than the 8 bit integer precision of NAV GSI.

name: NAV GLIDE SLOPE LENGTH
desc: The distance between the plane and the Glide beacon.

name: NAV GSI:1
desc: Glideslope needle deflection (+/- 119). Note that this provides only 8 bit precision, whereas NAV GLIDE SLOPE ERROR provides 32 bit floating point precision. Index of 1-4, depending on how many were defined in the Nav.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Navigation Index): :1, :2 …]

name: NAV GS FLAG:1
desc: Glideslope flag. Index of 1-4, depending on how many were defined in the Nav.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Navigation Index): :1, :2 …]

name: NAV NAME:1

name: NAV RAW GLIDE SLOPE

name: NAV SIGNAL
desc: Nav signal strength.

name: NAV SOUND:1
desc: Nav audio flag. Index of 1-4, depending on how many were defined in the Nav.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Navigation Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN ACTIVE CHANNEL:1
desc: The active channel used by the indexed Tacan receiver on the aircraft, from 1 to 127. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN ACTIVE MODE:1
desc: The active mode used by the indexed Tacan receiver on the aircraft, where 0 = X and 1 = Y . Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN AVAILABLE:1
desc: Will be TRUE (1) if NAV1, NAV2, NAV3 or NAV4 can receive the indexed Tacan , or FALSE (0) otherwise. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

desc: Tells whether the Tacan is driving the Nav 1 indicator ( TRUE , 1) or not ( FALSE , 0), for autopilot purposes.

name: TACAN OBS:1

name: TACAN STANDBY CHANNEL:1
desc: The standby channel used by the indexed Tacan receiver on the aircraft, from 1 to 127. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN STANDBY MODE:1
desc: Indicates the indexed Tacan receiver standby mode, where 0 = X and 1 = Y . Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN STATION CDI:1
desc: The CDI needle deflection amount (course deviation) to the indexed Tacan station. Can be +/- 127. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN STATION DISTANCE:1
desc: The distance between the indexed Tacan station position and the aircraft position. The index value refers to the Tacan receiver connected to the station. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN STATION RADIAL:1

name: TACAN STATION RADIAL ERROR:1
desc: Difference between the current radial and OBS tuned radial of the indexed Tacan station, in degrees. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . Degrees. [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

name: TACAN STATION TOFROM:1
desc: Returns whether the indexed Tacan is going to or from the current radial (or is off). Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …; 0 = Off; 1 = TO; 2 = FROM]

name: TACAN VOLUME:1
desc: The volume value of the indexed Tacan receiver on the aircraft. Index of 1 or 2, depending on how many were defined in the Tacan.N parameter of the systems.cfg . [indexed (Tacan Index): :1, :2 …]

If this variable returns true, it means that the latitude and longitude of the aircraft are not being controlled by the simulation, so enabling, for example, a SimConnect client to control the position of the aircraft. desc: Returns the current activity status of the named Fan . [indexed (Fan Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS FAN TARGET STATUS:1
desc: Returns the target activity status of the named Fan . [indexed (Fan Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS FAN SWITCH:1
desc: Whether or not the named Fan is active (1, TRUE) or not (0, FALSE). [indexed (Fan Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS JUNCTION LINE OPENING STATUS:1
desc: The opening status of a line onto a junction. Index 1 is the Junction index, and index 2 is the Line index. [indexed ([0] Junction index; [1] Line Index): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW:1
desc: The current airflow rate of the named Pack , expressed as a Percent Over 100 .; Note : This SimVar is settable, but any changes will be overridden by the simulation on the very next update frame. [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW AUTO:1
desc: Whether or not the named Pack airflow is handled automatically (1, TRUE) or not (0, FALSE). [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW MODE:1
desc: The current airflow mode of the named Pack . [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; 0 = Low; 1 = Normal; 2 = High]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW MODE VALUE:1
desc: The current airflow rate for the named pack using a given flow mode. Index 1 is the Pack index, and index 2 is the flow mode to check, one of the following:; 0 = Low; 1 = Normal; 2 = High [indexed ([0] Pack Name (or index); [1] Mode): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW MODE VALUE HIGH:1
desc: The airflow rate for the named Pack on the high flow mode. [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW MODE VALUE LOW:1
desc: The airflow rate for the named Pack on the low flow mode. [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK FLOW MODE VALUE NORM:1
desc: The airflow rate for the named Pack on the normal flow mode. [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK STATUS:1
desc: The current status of the named Pack , either enabled (1, TRUE), or disabled (0, FALSE). [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK SWITCH:1
desc: The status of the switch for the named Pack , either on (1, TRUE), or off (0, FALSE). [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS PACK TEMPERATURE:1
desc: The current temperature output of the named Pack . [indexed (Pack Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS TARGET CABIN ALTITUDE
desc: The target pressure altitude of the aircraft cabin.

name: PNEUMATICS VALVE MODE:1
desc: The current mode of the named Valve . [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; 0 = Open; 1 = Auto; 2 = Closed]

name: PNEUMATICS VALVE STATUS:1
desc: The current amount that the named Valve is open, expressed as a Percent Over 100 . [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PNEUMATICS VALVE TARGET STATUS:1
desc: The target amount that the named Valve should open to, expressed as a Percent Over 100 . [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: PNEUMATICS VALVE SWITCH:1
desc: Whether or not the named Valve is set to be opened (1, TRUE) or not (0, FALSE). [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PRESSURE ALTITUDE
desc: Standard Altitude, ie: at a 1013.25 hPa (1 atmosphere) setting.

name: PRESSURIZATION CABIN ALTITUDE
desc: The current altitude of the cabin pressurization.

name: PRESSURIZATION CABIN ALTITUDE GOAL
desc: The set altitude of the cabin pressurization as initialised from the design_cabin_pressure value in the systems.cfg file. Pressure is converted into an altitude using a standard condition table.; You can adjust the goal pressure using the PRESSURIZATION_PRESSURE_ALT_INC and PRESSURIZATION_PRESSURE_ALT_DEC events.

name: PRESSURIZATION CABIN ALTITUDE RATE
desc: The rate at which cabin pressurization changes.

name: PRESSURIZATION DUMP SWITCH
desc: True if the cabin pressurization dump switch is on.

name: PRESSURIZATION PRESSURE DIFFERENTIAL
desc: The difference in pressure between the current cabin pressure and the ambient pressure.

name: PARTIAL PANEL ADF
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL AIRSPEED
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL ALTIMETER
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL ATTITUDE
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL AVIONICS:1
desc: Will return a value depending on the availability of electrical power to the named (or indexed 💡︎ ) Circuit of the type CIRCUIT_AVIONICS . [indexed (v2+: Circuit name (or index) ; ; v1.00: Circuit index ; ; FSX: N/A): :1, :2 …; 0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL COMM
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL COMPASS
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL ELECTRICAL:1
desc: Will return a value depending on the availability of electrical power to the named (or indexed 💡︎ ) Circuit of the type CIRCUIT_GENERAL_PANEL . [indexed (v2+: Circuit name (or index) ; ; v1.00: Circuit index ; ; FSX: N/A): :1, :2 …; 0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL ENGINE
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL FUEL INDICATOR
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank]

name: PARTIAL PANEL HEADING
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL NAV
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL PITOT
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL TRANSPONDER
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL TURN COORDINATOR
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank]

name: PARTIAL PANEL VACUUM
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: PARTIAL PANEL VERTICAL VELOCITY
desc: Gauge fail flag. [0 = ok; 1 = fail; 2 = blank; settable]

name: DROPPABLE OBJECTS COUNT:1
desc: The number of droppable objects at the station number identified by the index. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: DROPPABLE OBJECTS TYPE:1
desc: The type of droppable object at the station number identified by the index. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: DROPPABLE OBJECTS UI NAME:1
desc: The descriptive name of a droppable object, identified by its index, which is used in UI dialogs. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PAYLOAD STATION COUNT
desc: Number of payload stations (1 to 15).

name: PAYLOAD STATION NAME:1
desc: Descriptive name for payload station. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PAYLOAD STATION NUM SIMOBJECTS:1
desc: The number of objects at the payload station. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PAYLOAD STATION OBJECT:1
desc: Places the named object at the payload station identified by the index (starting from 1). The string is the Container name (refer to the title property of Simulation Object Configuration Files). [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: PAYLOAD STATION WEIGHT:1
desc: Individual payload station weight. [indexed (Station Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: GRAPPLE HOOK SET
desc: This will return how open the grapple hook is, expressed as a Percent Over 100 where 0 is fully closed and 1 is fully open. [settable]

name: LEAD POLE SET
desc: This will return how far the lead pole is extended, expressed as a Percent Over 100 where 0 is no extension and 1 is fully extended. [settable]

name: TOW CABLE RELEASE REASON
desc: This will return the reason for which the tow cable was released. [0: none; 1: other; 2: user input; 3: winch at maximum angle; 4: towplane has crashed; 5: towplane in unsafe position; 6: towplane end of climb]

name: TOW CABLE TENSION
desc: The tension within the tow cable expressed as a Percent Over 100 , where 0 is no tension, and 1 is full tension.

name: TOW CONNECTION
desc: This will return 1 (TRUE) if a towline is connected to both the tow plane or winch and the glider, or 0 (FALSE) otherwise.

name: TOW PLANE CONNECTION
desc: This will return 1 (TRUE) if a towline is connected to both a tow plane and the glider, or 0 (FALSE) otherwise.

name: TOW RELEASE HANDLE
desc: This will return the position of the tow release handle, expressed as Percent Over 100 , where 0 is not deployed and 1 is fully deployed.

name: TOW WINCH CONNECTION
desc: This will return 1 (TRUE) if a towline is connected to both a winch and the glider, or 0 (FALSE) otherwise.

name: TAILHOOK HANDLE
desc: This will return 1 (TRUE) if the tailhook handle is engaged, or 0 (FALSE) otherwise.

name: TAILHOOK POSITION
desc: The amount that the tailhook is extended expressed as a Percent Over 100 , where 0 is the tailhook is not extended at all, and 1 is the tail hook fully extended. [settable]

name: NIGHT VISION AVAILABLE
desc: Will return whether the aircraft pilot has night vision (1, TRUE) or not (0, FALSE).

name: NIGHT VISION DISPLAYED
desc: Can be use to get or set whether the night vision display is on (1, TRUE) or off (0, FALSE). [settable]

name: NIGHT VISION INTENSITY
desc: Can be used to get or set the intensity of the night vision effect. When setting the intensity, values should be between 0 (lowest intensity) and 300 (highest intensity). [settable]

name: EXIT OPEN
desc: Percent door/exit open. [settable]

name: EXIT POSX
desc: Position of exit relative to datum reference point.

name: EXIT POSY
desc: Position of exit relative to datum reference point.

name: EXIT POSZ
desc: Position of exit relative to datum reference point.

name: EXIT TYPE
desc: The exit type. [0 = Main; 1 = Cargo; 2 = Emergency; 3 = Unknown]

name: BALLOON AUTO FILL ACTIVE
desc: Sets / returns whether the balloon is creating air inside to emulate fans air flow or not. [settable]

name: BALLOON FILL AMOUNT
desc: This is used to get / set the ratio of air within the balloon envelope from 0 (empty) to 1 (full). [settable]

name: BALLOON GAS DENSITY
desc: The density of the gas inside the balloon.

name: BALLOON GAS TEMPERATURE
desc: Temperature of the gas inside a balloon. [settable]

name: BALLOON VENT OPEN VALUE
desc: This represents how open the “parachute valve” of a hot air balloon is, where 0 is fully closed and 1 is fully open. [settable]

name: BURNER FUEL FLOW RATE:1
desc: The amount of fuel that is flowing through the named Burner expressed in lbs per hour. [indexed (Burner Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: BURNER HEATING POWER:1
desc: This is the thermal power of the named (or indexed) Burner expressed in BTU per hour. If a value of 0 is given instead of a name (or index) then the sum total of all burners heating power will be returned. [indexed (Burner Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: BURNER PILOT LIGHT ON:1
desc: The named (or indexed) hot air balloon Burner pilot light status, where 0 (FALSE) is off, and 1 (TRUE) is on. Note that of the burner is not receiving fuel this SimVar will revert to 0 (FALSE), if set to 1 (TRUE). [indexed (Burner Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: BURNER VALVE OPEN VALUE:1
desc: This represents how open the the named (or indexed) burner Valve is, where 0 is fully closed and 1 is fully open. [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: GROUND ATTACHMENT
desc: This toggles the status of the attachment rope. When 1 (true) the balloon has an attachment rope, and when 0 (false) it does not. [settable]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT GAS TYPE:1
desc: Gets the type of gas being used by the named (or indexed) gas compartment . [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; 0:Other; 1:Air; 2:Helium; 3:Hydrogen]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT OVERPRESSURE:1
desc: Gets the over-pressure value of the named (or indexed) gas compartment .; Note that this value is commonly expressed using inWG , which is not a supported SimVar unit, therfore some conversion may need done on the value before display/use. [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT PRESSURE:1
desc: Gets the current pressure value of the named (or indexed) gas compartment .; Note that this value is commonly expressed using inWG , which is not a supported SimVar unit, therfore some conversion may need done on the value before display/use. [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT TEMPERATURE:1
desc: Gets the current temperature value of the named (or indexed) gas compartment . [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT VOLUME:1
desc: Gets the volume of gas in the named (or indexed) gas compartment . [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: AIRSHIP COMPARTMENT WEIGHT:1
desc: Gets the weight of gas in the named (or indexed) gas compartment . [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …]

name: AIRSHIP DAMPER STATE:1
desc: Gets or sets the state of the named (or indexed) gas compartment damper.; Note that dampers are not defined explicitly, but are added automatically by the simulation, one per-compartment that is of the gas type “Air”. Non-air compartments do not have dampers. [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; 0:Locked; 1:Unlocked; 2:Forced Open; settable]

name: AIRSHIP FAN POWER PCT:1
desc: Gets or sets the state of the air intake fan for the named (or indexed) gas compartment .; Note that air intake fans are not defined explicitly, but are added automatically by the simulation, one per-compartment that is of the gas type “Air”. Non-air compartments do not have air intake fans. [indexed (Gas Compartment Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: AIRSHIP VALVE STATE:1
desc: Gets or sets the state of the named (or indexed) valve . [indexed (Valve Name (or index)): :1, :2 …; 0:Locked; 1:Unlocked; 2:Forced Open; settable]

name: MAST TRUCK DEPLOYMENT
desc: This toggles the status of the mast truck. When 1 (true) the truck should deploy the mast and other stabilisers, and when 0 (false) it should retract the mast and other stabilisers. [settable]

name: MAST TRUCK EXTENSION
desc: This is used to get / set the extension value of the mast from the mast truck (which needs to be deployed first), where a value of 0 is no extension and a value of 100 is full extension. [settable]

name: CAMERA GAMEPLAY PITCH YAW:1
desc: Returns either the pitch ( index 0 ) or the yaw ( index 1 ) of the current gameplay camera. [indexed (Pitch / Yaw): :1, :2 …]

name: CAMERA REQUEST ACTION
desc: This can be used to have the currently active camera perform a predefined action. Currently only 1 action is supported, but more may be added over time. [1 = Reset Active Camera (in VR this will recenter the headset view); 2 = Move Active Camera; settable]

name: CAMERA STATE
desc: This can be used to get or set the camera “state”, which will be one of the listed enum values.; Note that not all poossible values will do anything as some belong to legacy systems no longer used in MSFS 2024 and others have been reserved for future expansion of the camera system.; Also note that the value “9” is a special case, generally used only when working with in-sim panels and is used to go to the showcase cameras, defaulting to the last selected camera within this section (Drone, Fixed or Environment). [1 = Forced Custom Target Position; 2 = Cockpit; 3 = Chase Plane Drone; 4 = Fixed On Plane; 5 = Environment 6DOF; 6 = Gameplay; 7 = Showcase; 8 = Drone Plane; 9 = Waiting; 10 = World Map; 11 = Hangar RTC; 12 = Hangar Custom; 13 = Menu RTC; 14 = In Game RTC; 15 = Replay; 16 = Drone Developer; 17 = Drone Top Down; 18 = Follow Actor; 19 = Hangar; 20 = Old Drone Plane; 21 = Chase F18 Plane; 22 = Ground; 23 = Follow Air Traffic Plane; 24 = First View; 25 = Drone Photo Mode; 26 = Third View; 27 = Transition; 28 = Catch Object; 29 = Idle; 30 = World Map Idle; 31 = Explore Flightpath Drone; 32 = Focus Location; 33 = Worldmap Transition; settable]

name: CAMERA SUBSTATE
desc: This variable can be used to get or set the camera “sub-state”. The options here are generally only required when working with the in-sim panel UI. Note that the “locked” and “unlocked” state will be changed automatically if the following SimVars have their values changed: COCKPIT CAMERA HEADLOOK , CHASE CAMERA HEADLOOK . [1 = Locked (Fixed look or chase lock - The camera is locked in position); 2 = Unlocked (Head look or Chase normal - The camera is “attached” to the mouse); 3 = Quickview (the camera is currently using a Quickview); 4 = Smart (The camera has Smart camera active); 5 = Instrument (The camera is focused on an instruments panel); settable]

name: CAMERA VIEW TYPE AND INDEX:1
desc: With this you can get or set both the type of view for the current camera, as well as the option index, which will be between 0 and the maximum index value (as retrieved using the CAMERA VIEW TYPE AND INDEX MAX SimVar). Supplying an index of 0 to the SimVar will get/set the type (from the selection of enum values listed), and using an index of 1 will get/set the option index, which is an integer value.; Please see the Notes On View Types And Indices section below for more information. [indexed (Camera Index): :1, :2 …; 0 = Unknown / default (External / Chase and Showcase / Drone / Fixed / Environment states); 1 = Pilot View (Cockpit State); 2 = Instruments (Cockpit State); 3 = Quickview (Cockpit State); 4 = Quickview External (External State); 5 = View (Showcase / Drone / Fixed / Environment states); or; Number (index = 1); settable]

name: CAMERA VIEW TYPE AND INDEX MAX:1
desc: This variable can get the number of option indices related to a specific camera view type. The index value supplied to the SimVar should be one of the camera view type Enum values (see CAMERA VIEW TYPE AND INDEX ), and the SimVar will return the number of options available for that camera type (counting from 1, so - for example - if the camera view type is “Quickview” and has 8 quickview settings, then CAMERA VIEW TYPE AND INDEX MAX:4 will return 8). Note that this value can be set after a flight has started, but it will have no effect since the number of camera options is initilaised once only and not updated (and the simulation may overwrite the value again even after setting it).; Please see the Notes On View Types And Indices section below for more information. [indexed (Camera Type Index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: DIRECTORS CUT CAMERA PITCH
desc: Gets/sets the pitch of the Director’s Cut camera gimbal. [settable]

name: DIRECTORS CUT CAMERA YAW
desc: Gets/sets the yaw of the Director’s Cut camera gimbal. [settable]

name: GAMEPLAY CAMERA FOCUS
desc: This gets/sets the focus for the camera zoom, which can be either manual, or auto. The setting affects both the Cockpit and the External (Chase) cameras.; The following SimVars can be used to get/set the level of zoom: COCKPIT CAMERA ZOOM or CHASE CAMERA ZOOM . [0 = Auto; 1 = Manual; settable]

name: IS CAMERA RAY INTERSECT WITH NODE:1
desc: This SimVar is used to check for a collision along a ray from the center of the user FOV and a model node. The available nodes that can be checked using this SimVar must be previously defined in the [CAMERA_RAY_NODE_COLLISION] of the cameras.cfg file. The SimVar requires a node index value between 1 and 10, corresponding to the node defined in the CFG file, and the SimVar will return 1 ( TRUE ) if there is a collision along the camera ray or 0 ( FALSE ) otherwise. You may also supply an index of 0 to perform a collision check for all defined nodes, in which case the SimVar will return 1 ( TRUE ) if there is a collision between the ray and any of the defined nodes. Supplying an index outside of the range of 1 to 10, or supplying an index for which no node has been defined, will return 0 ( FALSE ). [indexed (Node): :1, :2 …]

name: CHASE CAMERA HEADLOOK
desc: This is used to get/set the look state of the chase (external) camera. Note that this value will also affect the CAMERA SUBSTATE value, when the CAMERA STATE is set to 3 (External/Chase). [1 = Freelook; 2 = Headlook; settable]

name: CHASE CAMERA MOMENTUM
desc: Sets/gets the momentum modifier of the chase (external) camera, which is controls how fast/slow the camera will stop moving when no longer being moved by the user. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: CHASE CAMERA SPEED
desc: Sets/gets the translation speed modifier of the chase (external) camera, as a percentage. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: CHASE CAMERA ZOOM
desc: Sets/gets the zoom/ FOV modifier for the chase (external) camera. Note that when setting this value, it will affect the camera regardless of whether the GAMEPLAY CAMERA FOCUS is set to manual or automatic. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: CHASE CAMERA ZOOM SPEED
desc: Sets/gets the speed modifier for when the zoom/ FOV chase (external) camera changes zoom/ FOV levels. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: CAMERA ACTION COCKPIT VIEW RESET
desc: This can be used to reset the cockpit camera when the CAMERA STATE is set to 2 (Cockpit). Essentially the same as the user pressing the default reset keys ⌃ Ctrl + ␣ Space . [settable]

name: CAMERA ACTION COCKPIT VIEW SAVE
desc: This can be used to save a cockpit camera when the CAMERA STATE is set to 2 (Cockpit). The index value given is the save “slot” that will be used, from 0 to 9. Essentially this is the same as the user pressing the default save keys ⌃ Ctrl + ⎇ Alt + 0 - 9 . [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA HEADLOOK
desc: This is used to get/set the look state of the cockpit camera. Note that this value will also affect the CAMERA SUBSTATE value, when the CAMERA STATE is set to 2 (Cockpit). [1 = Freelook; 2 = Headlook; settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA HEIGHT
desc: This can be used to get/set the cockpit camera height modifier expressed as a percentage. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA INSTRUMENT AUTOSELECT
desc: This can be used to get or set the autoselect option for the cockpit camera when viewing the instruments (ie: the CAMERA SUBSTATE is 5). When enabled the camera will move automatically if the player mouse reaches the edge of the screen and there are instrument panels available on that side. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA MOMENTUM
desc: Sets/gets the momentum modifier of the cockpit camera, which is controls how fast/slow the camera will stop moving when no longer being moved by the user. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA SIDE
desc: Not currently used in the simulation.

name: COCKPIT CAMERA SPEED
desc: Sets/gets the translation speed modifier of the cockpit camara, as a percentage. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA UPPER POSITION
desc: Sets/gets the current “upper position” cockpit camera toggle. When 1 ( TRUE ), the camera is is in the upper position, and when 0 ( FALSE ) it is in the default position. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA ZOOM
desc: Sets/gets the zoom/ FOV modifier for the cockpit camera. Note that when setting this value, it will affect the camera regardless of whether the GAMEPLAY CAMERA FOCUS is set to manual or automatic. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: COCKPIT CAMERA ZOOM SPEED
desc: Sets/gets the speed modifier for when the zoom/ FOV cockpit camera changes zoom/ FOV levels. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA FOCUS
desc: Sets/gets the focus modifier for the drone camera. Default is 50%, and a lower value will set the drone focus to things in the foreground and a higher level will set the drone focus to things in the background. Note that this is only taken into account when the DRONE CAMERA FOCUS MODE is set to 3 (manual). [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA FOCUS MODE
desc: Sets/gets the current drone focus mode. When set to 3 (manual), the focus position will be based on the [ DRONE CAMERA FOCUS ](#DRONE CAMERA FOCUS) value. [1 = Deactivated; 2 = Auto; 3 = Manual; settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA FOLLOW
desc: Sets/gets the whether the drone camera is in follow mode or not. [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA FOV
desc: Sets/gets the zoom/ FOV modifier for the drone camera. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA LOCKED
desc: Sets/gets the whether the drone camera is locked or not. [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA SPEED ROTATION
desc: Sets/gets the rotation speed modifier of the drone camara, as a percentage. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: DRONE CAMERA SPEED TRAVELLING
desc: Sets/gets the translation speed modifier of the drone camara, as a percentage. Default is 50%. [settable]

name: SMART CAMERA ACTIVE
desc: Sets/gets the whether the smart camera is active or not. [settable]

name: SMART CAMERA INFO:1
desc: Gets information on the smartcam system. The index sets what kind of information will be returned (or set):; 0 = Gets the number of smartcam targets in the smart camera list; 1 = Gets or sets the index of the currently selected smartcam target, counting from 0 (so index 0 is the first target in the list). [indexed (Camera Index): :1, :2 …; settable]

name: SMART CAMERA LIST:1
desc: Retrieves the type of target for the indexed position in the smartcam list, counting from 0 (so index 0 is the first target in the list). [indexed (Camera Index): :1, :2 …; 0 = unknown POI; 1 = Follow POI; 2 = User POI; 3 = General POI; 4 = End OF Runway; 5 = Landing Runway; 6 = Flightpath; 7 = Object Interaction; 8 = Multiplayer OOI; 9 = Active Runway; 10 = Waypoint; 11 = Airport OOI; 12 = Flight Assistant Destination]

name: SMART CAMERA LIST DESCRIPTION:1
desc: This returns a localized string that represents the smartcam target specified by the given index. Indices count from 0 so index 0 is the first target in the list. [indexed (Camera Index): :1, :2 …]

name: COLLECTIVE POSITION
desc: The position of the helicopter collective. 0 is fully up, 1 fully depressed.

name: VORTEX RING STATE PROTECTION ASSISTANCE IMPACT
desc: Indicates how much the current collective lever position has been increased by the vortex ring state protection assistance, compared to the user input. See Note On Helicopter Vortex Ring Protection Assistance for more information.

name: DISK BANK ANGLE:1
desc: Rotor bank angle of the given engine index rotor.; The SimVar takes an index value, which is the index of the rotor to target. Note that an index of 0 will target the first rotor.; NOTE : This is available in multiplayer to all far aircraft. See here for more information: Note On SimVars In Multiplayer . [indexed (Engine Index 💡︎): :1, :2 …]

name: DISK BANK PCT:1

name: FREEWHEELING UNIT ENGAGED:1
desc: Indicates whether the indexed engine freewheeling unit is engaged and transmitting torque to the rotor system (1, TRUE), or disengaged/freewheeling (0, FALSE). Engines that are disconnected from the transmission will no longer contribute shaft torque to the rotor system. Their RPM is no longer updated internally and can be controlled externally via the GENERAL ENG RPM SimVar (without external writes, it will remain unchanged). Connected engines will continue to use the existing clutch and transmission simulation.; NOTE : This SimVar has the following constraints:; FWU engagement and disengagement are discrete and instantaneous. There is no slipping phase, RPM synchronization, or transient engagement torque.; When an FWU is engaged while the engine is running at a different RPM, the engine is immediately set to the shared engine speed. This is physically incorrect and can create or remove kinetic energy.; When several engines are connected, a single shared RPM is selected. Sometimes it is taken from the first engine, and sometimes it is the maximum RPM of the connected engines. This is inconsistent and can cause RPM jumps. ; As a result, reconnecting an engine may cause its immediate RPM change. These transitions will therefore need to be managed on the aircraft side. name: JETWAY WHEEL ORIENTATION TARGET
desc: The (approximate) target angle for the jetway wheels. [settable]

name: JETWAY WHEEL SPEED
desc: The current speed of the jetway wheels. [settable]

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT DIRECTION PARKINGSPACE
desc: Currently not used in the simulation.

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT DISTANCE
desc: The distance between the Marshaller and the aircraft.

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT DISTANCE DIRECTION X PARKINGSPACE
desc: Position on the X axis of the aircraft in the parking space (negative means the aircraft is on the left side and positive the right side).

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT DISTANCE DIRECTION Z PARKINGSPACE
desc: Position on the Z axis of the aircraft in the parking space (negative means the aircraft is behind the parking space and positive is in front of the parking space).

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT ENGINE SHUTDOWN
desc: True if the engine(s) of the aircraft is (are) shut down.

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT HEADING PARKINGSPACE
desc: Angle between the direction of the aircraft and the direction of the parking place.

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT PROJECTION POINT PARKINGSPACE
desc: Value in Z axis of the projection from the aircraft position following the heading of the aircraft.

name: MARSHALLER AIRCRAFT VELOCITY
desc: The velocity of the aircraft.

name: PUSHBACK ANGLE
desc: Pushback angle (the heading of the tug).

name: PUSHBACK ATTACHED
desc: True if this vehicle is attached to an aircraft. [settable]

name: PUSHBACK AVAILABLE
desc: True if a push back is available on the parking space. [settable]

name: PUSHBACK CONTACTX
desc: The towpoint position, relative to the aircrafts datum reference point.

name: PUSHBACK CONTACTY
desc: Pushback contact position in vertical direction.

name: PUSHBACK CONTACTZ
desc: Pushback contact position in fore/aft direction.

name: PUSHBACK STATE
desc: Type of pushback. [0 = Straight; 1 = Left; 2 = Right; settable]

name: PUSHBACK WAIT
desc: True if waiting for pushback.

name: WAGON BACK LINK LENGTH
desc: The length of the link at the back of the vehicle used to attach a wagon behind.

name: WAGON BACK LINK ORIENTATION
desc: The current orientation of the link at the back of the vehicle used to attach a wagon behind. [settable]

name: WAGON BACK LINK START POSZ
desc: The “Z” axis position of the start of the link at the back of the vehicle used to attach a wagon behind, relative to the ground.

name: WAGON FRONT LINK LENGTH
desc: The length of the link at the front of the vehicle used to be attached as wagon.

name: WAGON FRONT LINK ORIENTATION
desc: The current orientation of the link at the front of the vehicle used to be attached as wagon. [settable]

name: WAGON FRONT LINK START POSZ
desc: The “Z” axis position of the start of the link at the front of the vehicle used to be attached as wagon, relative to the ground.

name: ABSOLUTE TIME
desc: This returns the seconds since 12:00 am 1/1/1AD Zulu Time ) See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU DAY OF WEEK
desc: This returns the current Zulu Time day of the week as an integer value between 0 and 6 (inclusive), where 0 is Sunday and 6 is Saturday. See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU DAY OF MONTH
desc: This returns the current Zulu Time day of the month as an integer value between 1 and 31 (inclusive). See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU MONTH OF YEAR
desc: This returns the current Zulu Time month of the year as an integer value between 1 and 12 (inclusive), where 1 is January and 12 is December. See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU DAY OF YEAR
desc: This returns the current Zulu Time day of the year as an integer value between 0 and 365 (365 only on a leap year). See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU YEAR
desc: This returns the current Zulu Time year as an integer value. See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU SUNRISE TIME
desc: This returns the seconds since midnight until the sunrise based on Zulu Time . See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: ZULU SUNSET TIME
desc: This returns the seconds since midnight until the sunset based on Zulu Time . See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: LOCAL DAY OF WEEK
desc: This returns the current day of the week as an integer value between 0 and 6 (inclusive), where 0 is Sunday and 6 is Saturday, within the local time reference.

name: LOCAL DAY OF MONTH
desc: This returns the current day of the month as an integer value between 1 and 31 (inclusive), within the local time reference.

name: LOCAL MONTH OF YEAR
desc: This returns the current month of the year as an integer value between 1 and 12 (inclusive), where 1 is January and 12 is December, within the local time reference.

name: LOCAL DAY OF YEAR
desc: This returns the current day of the year as an integer value between 0 and 365 (365 only on a leap year), within the local time reference.

name: LOCAL YEAR
desc: This returns the current year (local time) as an integer value.

name: TIME ZONE OFFSET
desc: This returns the offset between the local time and Zulu Time . See the Note On Zulu Time for more information.

name: TIME OF DAY
desc: This will return an integer value representing the approximate time of day where:; 0 = dawn; 1 = day; 2 = dusk; 3 = night [(Number)]

name: TOOLTIP UNITS
desc: This will return an integer value representing the current units used to display tooltip information, where:; 0 = default; 1 = metric (SI); 2 = US (imperial) [(Number)]

name: UNITS OF MEASURE
desc: This indicates the units used to express measurements and will return an integer value representing the following:; 0 - English; 1 - Metric with altitude in feet; 2 - Metric with altitude in meters [(Number)]

name: SIMULATION TIME
desc: This returns a value for the seconds since the simulation has been started.

name: SIMULATION DELTA TIME
desc: This returns a value for the time passed between the last simulation frame and the current one.

name: IS IN VR
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the simulation is in VR mode or not.

name: IS USING MOTION CONTROLLERS
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the user is using 6DoF controllers in VR or not.

name: IS USING JOYSTICK THROTTLE
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the user is manipulating the throttle with a joystick device or not.

name: IS IN RTC
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the simulation is currently running an RTC or not.

name: IS AVATAR
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the user is in “Avatar” mode or not.

name: IS AIRCRAFT
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the user is in “Aircraft” mode or not.

name: IS CAMERA LOCKED
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether the camera is locked or not.

name: EFB BRIGHTNESS
desc: This return the brightness of the EFB , from 0 to 1. If it is set to “auto brightness” within the EFB’s settings, then -1 will be returned.

name: SWITCH USER ALWAYS ALLOWED
desc: This returns either 1 (TRUE) or 0 (FALSE) to indicate whether there is no limitation to switch between avatar and aircraft mode or not.
